$comment: jitLLM's source lock (D-017, D-057): every third-party source component a build may use, with its exact bytes, license classification and build options. third_party/README.md describes the schema and how to change it.
`mise run prepare` fetches and unpacks the selected components into build/sources; configure (cmake/JitllmSources.cmake) only consumes those trees and writes the build receipt.

license.scope: Compiled, by jitllm/CMakeLists.txt (added by patches/ggml/0002-jitllm-build.patch) and never by GGML's own CMake: ggml/src/ggml.c, ggml-alloc.c, ggml-backend.cpp, ggml-backend-meta.cpp, ggml-quants.c and ggml-threading.cpp (target jitllm_ggml_base, every profile), and in CUDA profiles ggml/src/ggml-cuda/binbcast.cu, convert.cu, cpy.cu, getrows.cu, mmf.cu, mmid.cu, mmvf.cu, norm.cu, rope.cu, set-rows.cu, softmax.cu, unary.cu and template-instances/mmf-instance-ncols_1.cu to _16.cu (target jitllm_ggml_cuda), with the headers they include from ggml/include, ggml/src (ggml-impl.h, ggml-common.h, ggml-quants.h, ggml-threading.h, ggml-backend-impl.h, ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu-impl.h) and ggml/src/ggml-cuda, and ggml-version.h generated from ggml/src/ggml-version.h.in; jitLLM's src/kernels/ggml/ includes the same headers. Executed at configure: jitllm/CMakeLists.txt only. archive.keep drops the rest of the archive (llama.cpp itself, GGML's CMake, CPU backend, other backends, ggml-cuda.cu's backend runtime is kept in ggml/src/ggml-cuda but not compiled). Not compiled from the kept tree: ggml-cuda.cu and every other ggml-cuda .cu file (flash attention, MMQ, MMVQ, the other operations); src/kernels/ggml/ggml_support.cu is jitLLM's adaptation of the ggml-cuda.cu functions the launchers need (MIT AND Apache-2.0).
license.evidence: Root LICENSE (SHA-256 94f29bbed6a22c35b992c5c6ebf0e7c92f13b836b90f36f461c9cf2f0f1d010d) is MIT, Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors; no compiled or included file carries its own license header, so all fall under it. ggml/src/ggml-cuda/rope.cu lines 20-21 attribute its YaRN rotation to https://github.com/jquesnelle/yarn, 'MIT licensed. Copyright (c) 2023 Jeffrey Quesnelle and Bowen Peng.' ggml/src/ggml-impl.h's FP16 conversion cites https://github.com/Maratyszcza/FP16 (MIT) by reference only, and its static_assert fallback cites a Stack Overflow answer for a one-line preprocessor idiom; neither retains a notice upstream. The archive's other trees (tools/ui's npm lock metadata names LGPL-3.0 packages; vendor/ holds MIT and public-domain code) are removed by archive.keep before patching and never built (checked 2026-09-26).
license.obligations: Linked so far only into test executables (the backend proof's P1), which are never shipped. A shipped binary that links it must carry GGML's MIT notice (LICENSE) and the YaRN copyright and license line from ggml/src/ggml-cuda/rope.cu in the package's third-party notices; jitLLM's ggml_support.cu carries the same GGML notice in its header. No source offer is owed.

ggml.verification: Pinned to llama.cpp tag b10964 (also v0.4.1), commit b29c606e28a01b1bc8c1351026a0fa6e616bf6c4, the revision of the FP16 reference and toolchain bridge (docs/experiments/first-slice/pins.json, docs/experiments/backend-proof-p0/). GitHub's archive of that commit was downloaded twice on 2026-09-26 with identical SHA-256 and size. tree_sha256 is the kept, patched tree, computed by the shared tools/jitllm_sources.py validator during preparation, configure and build. The patches (third_party/patches/ggml/) change behaviour only when GGML_JITLLM is defined, which only jitllm/CMakeLists.txt defines. The build reproduces the bridge's flags for these files (-O3, sm_121a SASS, -use_fast_math, -extended-lambda, C11/C++17 host code, C++17 CUDA); the bridge's compile commands are the reference.

Executed at configure: CMakeLists.txt, googletest/CMakeLists.txt, googlemock/CMakeLists.txt and googletest/cmake/internal_utils.cmake. license.scope: Compiled: include/toml++/toml.hpp and the include/toml++/impl/ headers it includes, in header-only mode, by one jitLLM translation unit (src/config/node_config.cc) with TOML_EXCEPTIONS=0, TOML_ENABLE_FORMATTERS=0 and TOML_ENABLE_UNRELEASED_FEATURES=0. license.evidence: Root LICENSE (SHA-256 529bc3900a9571e49db285b0df432397e70b881cc3bf48de6667ae74ff4b06d8) is MIT, Copyright (c) Mark Gillard. Every header under include/toml++/impl/ and include/toml++/toml.hpp carries Mark Gillard's MIT header with an SPDX identifier for MIT except header_start.hpp, header_end.hpp and toml.h, which have none and fall under the root LICENSE, as do the CMake scripts. impl/unicode.hpp's UTF-8 decoder is based on Bjoern Hoehrmann's DFA decoder and keeps its line 'Copyright (c) 2008-2009 Bjoern Hoehrmann' (published by its author under the MIT license). impl/unicode_autogenerated.hpp holds character-class functions that toml++'s tools generated from Unicode character data; in TOML 1.0.0 mode only the horizontal and vertical whitespace classes (ASCII and non-ASCII) and the ASCII bare-key class are compiled; the Unicode bare-key tables are not. license.obligations: Linked into the shipped jitllm binaries (the node configuration). Binary redistribution must include toml++'s MIT notice (copyright and permission notice) and Bjoern Hoehrmann's copyright line from impl/unicode.hpp in the package's third-party notices. Its Unicode-derived tables fall under the Unicode notice question in licensing.md (open decision 4). No source offer is owed.

tomlplusplus.verification: Pinned to master commit 1e8829b793b66ad17011732a146b8077d379b011 (2026-07-21), 50 commits after v3.4.0 (2023-10-13), the last tagged release, because those commits fix input-reachable defects: a stack overflow from deeply dotted keys (#242), a stack overflow from deeply nested arrays and inline tables (1c8b7466), a precondition violation on '[[[' table headers (#301) and undefined behaviour formatting fractional doubles (#276). GitHub's archive of that commit was downloaded twice on 2026-09-24 with identical SHA-256 and size. tree_sha256 is the FetchContent-unpacked tree, computed by the shared tools/jitllm_sources.py validator during preparation, configure and build. Its parser was checked on 2026-09-24 to reject duplicate keys, redefined tables, integers outside 64 bits, leading zeros, unescaped control characters and invalid UTF-8, with -fno-exceptions (tests/unit/config_test.cc keeps the cases jitLLM relies on).
